risks.risk: Transition risk from integration with JSW Group
risks.note: The ongoing transition of JSW Dulux into the JSW Group creates customer-continuity concerns around product quality, warranties, formulations and global technology access, and operational/IT transition activities (including phased ERP/applications migration) may create temporary business disruption if not tightly controlled.

Global geopolitical uncertainties are causing price fluctuations, availability challenges and longer lead times for several imported materials, which can lead to cost escalation, margin pressure and potential delays in production planning/stock coverage.

The Company is encountering challenges in both retaining and attracting customers, vendors and employees amid the strategic transition, requiring active relationship-strengthening measures across all three groups.

Manufacturing processes carry inherent risks of injury and occupational hazards from exposure to harmful materials/waste, mitigated through the Company's HSES policy, training and periodic risk assessments.

risks.risk: Security, cyber and information control systems
risks.note: Insufficient information security/cybersecurity systems — driven by end-user awareness gaps, tooling limitations and increasingly sophisticated attackers — pose risk of loss of sensitive information, intellectual property, banking data, business disruption and reputational damage; this extends to data-privacy compliance risk more broadly.

A continually evolving local regulatory environment is increasing regulatory scrutiny and stakeholder compliance expectations; non-compliance poses a threat to the Company's financial and reputational standing.

Market competition and a fast-evolving business environment create challenges in attracting and retaining talent, addressed through focused acquisition strategy, retention rewards and employee engagement.

risks.risk: Loss of market share to competition
risks.note: Intensifying competition and new entrants, including digital disruption, risk eroding market share in certain segments; mitigation centres on dealer-profitability competitiveness, brand investment and expanding numeric/geographic reach.

one_liner.body: JSW Dulux Limited (formerly Akzo Nobel India), now 61.2%-owned by JSW Paints, is a paints and coatings manufacturer combining the legacy Dulux brand with JSW Group scale across Decorative Paints, Industrial Paints (Marine & Protective Coatings, Automotive & Specialty Coatings) and Coil & Packaging …

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures and supplies paints, varnishes, enamels and lacquers across decorative and industrial end-uses, sold through a distributor/dealer network reaching over 5,000 towns and 22,000+ dealers. Its industrial portfolio spans Marine & Protective Coatings (anti-corrosive/anti-fouling solutions for naval and maritime vessels, Oil & Gas, Power, Mining, Infrastructure and Wind Energy), Automotive & Specialty Coatings (Vehicle Refinish, Automotive Plastic Coatings, Specialty Coatings for OEM and Consumer Electronics) and Coil & Extrusion / Metal Packaging Coatings for building & construction, infrastructure, appliances and metal packaging.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- ICI India Research & Technology Centre Private Limited — subsidiary: 99.99% shareholding, per Form AOC-1 Part A
- Akzo Nobel Powder Coatings India Private Limited — related party: Previously a group entity; counterparty to the slump sale of the Company's Powder Coatings business and International Research Centre operations
- Akzo Nobel Coatings International BV — related party: Erstwhile Holding/Promoter company; counterparty for the Company's acquisition of intellectual property rights (including the Dulux brand) pertaining to the Decorative Paints business in India, Bhutan, Bangladesh & Nepal, an arrangement ongoing till December 2026

products.body:

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Rapid urbanisation: urban population in India expected to touch 600 million by 2031, driving residential demand
- Government infrastructure push: sustained public-sector spending on roads, bridges and transport, supported by a record Budget capex outlay
- Real estate momentum: expansion of affordable housing and 'ready-to-move' homes, supported by PMAY
- Rising middle class: growing disposable income and aspiration for premium home finishes, with the Indian middle class now comprising 31% of the population
- Industrial growth: strong bounce-back in manufacturing, energy, auto production and metallurgy driving demand for high-performance industrial and protective coatings
- Shift towards sustainable products: growing environmental awareness, green building adoption and stricter emission norms accelerating demand for eco-friendly, low-VOC and water-based paints and coatings
- EV ecosystem growth: rising EV registrations and penetration driving demand for high-performance coatings in battery packs and mobility components
- Shorter repainting cycles: consumers increasingly inclined toward repainting services, shifting the industry toward a service-oriented ecosystem
- Modular furniture growth driving demand for sophisticated wood finish and adhesive products
- Decorative segment continues to lead the paints market (approximately 75% of total demand) while the industrial segment (approximately 25%) is driven by automotive recovery and energy/metallurgy demand
- Decorative Paints demand was muted with heightened competitive pressures in H1 FY26, followed by a strong recovery in H2 FY26
- Headwinds flagged: fluctuations in raw material prices, existing and emerging geopolitical situations, and stringent VOC-related environmental regulations
- Opportunities flagged: use of nanotechnology in paints/coatings and rising demand for eco-friendly paints expected to offer market growth opportunities
- Competitive intensity in decorative paints continues to rise as established players increase capex on dealer networks and manufacturing capabilities amid new entrants
- Vehicle Refinish Coatings secured 150+ new bodyshop wins in FY26 and received exclusive Porsche India network approval
- Established exclusive partnerships, most notably with JSW MG Motor India, positioning the Company as a primary supplier for next-generation mobility
- Strengthened the Automotive Plastics Coatings business with a leading Indian automotive OEM, driving multi-fold revenue growth in FY26 on products developed at the Bengaluru R&D facility
- Expanded exclusive partnership with Mahindra for Auto Interiors across new car models

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin expanded to 18.5% (from 16.8% YoY) despite 9% YoY rise in titanium dioxide and resin costs; 120 bps margin gain from pricing and mix optimization

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Dividend payout of ₹12/share (₹1,200cr total); ₹420cr capex; ₹100cr for potential M&A; net cash position maintained

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company operates five manufacturing facilities and, during FY26, initiated preparations for cross-manufacturing of products for the JSW group, with Phase 1 beginning between its Gwalior site and JSW Paints' Vijayanagar site to enhance operational integration and service efficiency. At the Gwalior site, productivity improvements raised In-Line Disperser (ILD) batches from 34 to 38 in a two-shift operation for two ILDs, and the Company is aiming for further capacity expansion there through the addition of two filling lines and associated equipment to support future demand growth. Separately, in the Automotive Plastics Coatings business, the Company is pursuing strategic capacity expansion initiatives including additional capex investments at its Bengaluru plant, alongside plans to widen the business into new segments such as commercial vehicles and paint consumables.

moat.body:
- Distribution reach of 22,000+ dealers and presence in over 5,000 towns, targeted to expand to over 6,000 towns
- Legacy Dulux brand equity backed by a 10-year Dulux Assurance warranty programme, reinforcing premium positioning and consumer trust
- Access to JSW Group scale, combined manufacturing capacity across multiple locations, and cross-group institutional relationships (e.g. exclusive supply partnerships with JSW MG Motor India) following the 61.2% stake acquisition by JSW Paints
- Long-standing technical/strategic relationships in Industrial Paints, including a strategic partnership with the Indian Navy for high-specification anti-corrosive and anti-fouling coatings
- Exclusive supplier relationships in Automotive Plastic/Interior coatings (e.g. expanded exclusive partnership with Mahindra for Auto Interiors; exclusive supplier of automotive interior coatings for premium EV models)

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Carve-out] The deck's like-for-like columns exclude a carved-out / AN-retained business, described as provisional, unaudited and based on Mgmt estimates — so the statutory and L2L prior-year bases differ materially and are not interchangeable.
- [Rename] The filing is signed for JSW Dulux Limited (Formerly Akzo Nobel India Limited), BSE scrip 500710 / NSE JSWDULUX.
- [Related entity] Deck attributes dividend income of 55.9 Cr in the quarter to ICI India Research and Technology Centre Private Limited, and separately notes interest on IT refund of 21.5 Cr — both non-operating items.
- [Group footnote] The JSW Group slides carry a footnote reading Further 4.5mtpa capacity in Joint Venture currently, growing to 16mtpa by FY32, with market caps as on 3rd June 2026; extraction loses which group entity that capacity belongs to, and it is not stated to be JSW Dulux capacity.
- [Macro backdrop] Deck frames the period as resilient growth amidst cost and currency volatilities — FY26 GDP growth intact, dip in consumer confidence, uptick in inflation with RBI target breached, and the rupee weighed down by FII outflows and crude.
